newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's CSP Int'l aims for Bourse quote by summer.
newsitem.headline: Italy's CSP Int'l aims for Bourse quote by summer.

text.p: Italian hosiery company CSP International, ranked second in the sector in the domestic market and fourth in Europe, hopes to be listed on the Milan stockmarket by summer, general manager Gianfranco Bossi said.

The flotation plan includes a capital increase and the sale of stakes by current shareholders. Founders of the Mantova-based company, the Bertoni brothers, hold 64 percent of the firm and will remain majority shareholders.
The rest will be offered by global coordinator UBS who came into the group in 1995 taking a 31.3 percent stake.
CSP, founded in 1972, specialises in ladies' stockings with the brands Sanpellegrino and Oroblu.
It posted 1996 net profit of 10.5 billion lire against 2.1 billion in 1995 on sales of 233.7 billion lire versus 191.3 billion.
Bossi said 1997 had begun well. Without giving figures, he told a press presentation that the pace of growth so far was in line with that of previous years.
Fresh funds deriving from the placement will in part finance planned investments equal to 45 billion lire over the next three years. Bossi said he did not rule out future acquisitions.
Lead manager of the public sale offer will be Cariplo, with co-lead Mediocredito Lombardo, and joint leads for a private placement are UBS and Cariplo.
